messages:
elena: noticed steady RSS growth on streaming chat with tool loops. ~30MB/hour for one worker. Starts after ~45k tokens, looks like KV pages not being reclaimed. attaching quick notes.

raj: ouch. which branch/runtime? any recent kernel selection changes? :thinking_face:

elena: main (release-2026-02). we rolled in the new continuous-batch kernel and the new kv-reclaim heuristic two weeks ago. suspected interaction.

ben: can you paste the pmap / jemalloc stats? also which model / seq len?

elena: model: redwood-v1-large, typical seq stream ~20-30k tokens over time (chat + tool loops that call model for each tool response).

elena: snapshot of rss over time from perf host: 
```
2026-06-01T09:00  RSS 1.2G
2026-06-01T12:00  RSS 1.26G
2026-06-01T15:00  RSS 1.34G
2026-06-01T18:00  RSS 1.44G
```

elena: jemalloc stats after 18:00: 
```
allocated: 980MB
active: 1.43GB
metadata: 40MB
resident: 1.44GB
retained: 200MB
arena_count: 28
```

raj: arena_count 28 seems high for 1 worker. maybe fragmentation across arenas after many evictions. any evidence of stale KV pages pinned?

elena: found this with pprof on heap: lots of small persistent allocations from kv_cache -> page_index objects. sample: 
```
# top 5 by alloc_size
kv_cache::PageIndex  180MB
kv_cache::CachedShard 120MB
protobuf::Message  60MB
std::string  40MB
```

ben: PageIndex 180MB is suspicious. Is reclaim triggered only on allocation pressure? maybe our heuristic defers reclamation because of batch size smoothing.

ops-metrics: we deployed metric kv.reclaim.calls= 8/day and kv.reclaim.evicted_pages= 24 yesterday on that host. reclaim latency median 120ms.

elena: interesting: evicted_pages is low compared to number of logical page rotations. I instrumented page touch counts and saw many pages with touch_count=0 for long periods (unused), but still retained by arenas. suspect free list not merged back to OS because of jemalloc retaining.

raj: two hypotheses: 1) our reclaim only clears page metadata but doesn't free underlying large buffers (we reuse buffer pools), 2) jemalloc retention + multiple arenas causes RSS growth even after free.

ben: do we have a repro? small local run that simulates long streaming chat + tool loop calling model repeatedly?

elena: yes. I ran a local sim for 24h. script: 
```
for i in $(seq 1 40000); do
  curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/generate -d '{"input":"question $i","stream":true}'
  sleep 0.02
done
```

elena: results: rss up +150MB vs cold start. heap profile shows incremental growth correlated with number of unique tool calls (each tool call creates a small metadata proto per span).

raj: maybe proto objects never get freed due to cycle or global caches? search for static singletons or global cache inserts on tool-path.

elena: found code: kv_cache::register_page_snapshot(...) stores a shared_ptr in a global LRU map for safety; intended to be short lived but eviction path only removes keys when pages hit a threshold (kv.reclaim.threshold=1024). For long contexts, many ephemeral pages accumulate below threshold.

ben: that sounds like the bug. The threshold logic optimized for throughput but not long tail token churn. Should we change to a time-based TTL or adaptive threshold based on touch recency?

elena: I prototyped a change: when touch_count==0 and last_access_ts > 10m -> immediate reclaim regardless of threshold. quick run: reclaimed ~70% of page_index objects, rss plateaued.

ops-metrics: rolling that to canary in stg shows kv.reclaim.calls increased x3 but evicted_pages x10, latency unaffected. metrics: request P95 latency +2ms.

raj: +2ms seems acceptable if it prevents unbounded memory growth. any regression tests?

elena: added unit tests around eviction TTL and a small integration test that runs long streaming workload for 1h and checks rss delta < 50MB.

ben: what about jemalloc arenas? Even after free, retained may stay. did you call mallctl to purge unused pages?

elena: good point. I added a background purge trigger: mallctl("arena.<id>.purge"). But we only call it when retained > 100MB to avoid overhead. In stg, purge calls were rare and work well.

elena: also disabled buffer pool reuse for page buffers older than 30m. That reduced retained from 200MB -> 40MB in canary.

ops-metrics: shoulder-check: canary logs show no OOMs and CPU tax for purge is negligible (~0.5%).

raj: ok let's prepare a careful rollout: patch -> canary with ttl reclaim + purge -> monitor rss + P99 latency + reclaim cost. If green, ship to prod. Add a feature flag to flip back fast.

ben: also open a follow-up to revisit kernel selection and batch smoothing: we should ensure batching heuristic exposes enough allocation pressure signals so reclaim isn't starved.

elena: created PR #4826 with tests. also filed perf task PERF-998 to evaluate kernel/batching interaction.

ci-bot: PR #4826 passed CI (unit+integration). deploy to canary started at 2026-06-02T02:30Z.

elena: thanks everyone. will keep an eye and post results. :rocket:
